static_dimensions.description: A static categorical attribute reflecting the primary diagnostic category and subtype of depression or relevant comorbid disorders identified at the start of therapy.
Enduring, broad, and deeply held beliefs about self, others, and the world that influence all aspects of cognition, emotion, and behavior.
Stable personality trait clusters or features impacting therapy, including tendencies toward perfectionism, dependence, avoidance, or emotional instability.
A default mode of processing information, indicating habitual patterns such as rumination, dichotomous thinking, attributional style, or emotional reasoning.
Relatively fixed preferences and expectations regarding therapy modalities, openness to psychological vs. pharmacological treatment, and stance toward collaboration.
Stable contextual factors such as age group, relationship status, employment, cultural or developmental context, and care setting, influencing engagement and accessibility.

dynamic_dimensions.description: A dynamic categorical state reflecting current mood and affective functioning, including both the presence and intensity of depressive, anxious, or other emotions.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Changes in response to symptom fluctuations, session events, interventions, homework completion, or external life stressors.

dynamic_dimensions.description: A dynamic state indicating the degree of participation, collaboration, and investment in the therapy process.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Can change with the quality of the therapeutic alliance, experience of progress/setbacks, personal motivation, or direct intervention by the therapist.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Dynamic patterns representing the current intensity and variety of cognitive distortions or automatic negative thoughts displayed.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Changes as patient acquires and applies cognitive skills, as mood improves or worsens, or during exposure to relevant triggering situations.

dynamic_dimensions.description: A state denoting current willingness to engage in change-oriented tasks, experiment with new behaviors, and tolerate discomfort.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Shifts with patient insight, experience of success or failure, crisis moments, intervention efficacy, and positive reinforcement from therapy.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Current level of engagement in adaptive activities versus avoidance or withdrawal behaviors.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Evolves as a function of behavioral experiments, external stressors or accomplishments, and shifts in mood or environmental support.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Dynamic state reflecting the current quality of the therapeutic relationship, the patient's trust, responsiveness to feedback, and likelihood of expressing relational concerns.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Alters following alliance-building interventions, ruptures or repairs in session, therapist feedback, or personal disclosures.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Level of follow-through with therapeutic assignments, practice of CBT skills, and response to in-session troubleshooting.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Ranges with mood, perceived relevance or difficulty of tasks, engagement in therapy, and outcome success or obstacles encountered.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Capacity for introspection, awareness of thoughts/feelings, and ability to identify cognitive-emotional links.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Improves with Socratic questioning, repeated self-monitoring, and feedback from therapist; may decrease with intense emotion or resistance.

dynamic_dimensions.description: Current risk for symptom relapse and level of preparedness to employ prevention strategies independently.
dynamic_dimensions.update_condition: Modifies with symptom stability, skill mastery, successful practice of relapse prevention plans, and response to life events or therapy termination.
